Interfaces

ContentActionSpec

A read-only action over the page's content rather than an entry ([S-AUTO-16]): read returns what the page shows the person, wait resolves when a condition on the page holds. It needs a surface that carries a page-content reader (autoSurface attaches one; a relay mirror forwards to the page's); on any other surface it is unavailable. It never acts and never moves the revision.

DomainActionSpec

One parameterized action of domainActions ([S-AXE-10]): a stable name, the application's own title and description, the entries it acts on, and risk metadata that holds for every one of them. The action takes { entryId, text?, confirm? } and runs the entry's own op through surface.act, exactly as the entry's per-control action would.

Properties

auth?
optional auth?: WireAuthMode;

Auth mode of this action; default the bridge's auth.

covers
covers: (entry) => boolean;

Which entries the action acts on. Asked once per registered entry object; an entry that more than one spec covers belongs to the first. Select by kind, by object or id prefix, or by effect.mutates: whatever makes a group the application would name.

Parameters
entry

Entry

Returns

boolean

description
description: string;

Composed into the action's description, before the bridge's sentence on entryId and refusals.

humanHandoff?
optional humanHandoff?: object;

The handoff reasons a covered control may return as needs_human (protocol humanHandoff). The per-control action derives it from the entry; a parameterized action cannot know its entries in advance, so the application declares it.

reasons
reasons: string[];

idempotent?
optional idempotent?: boolean;

True only when every covered entry is idempotent; an entry that is not is left uncovered. Default false.

idleReason?
optional idleReason?: string;

The availability reason when no entry the action covers can be acted on now (and the surface is not frozen, when the freeze's reason is reported instead). Default: "nothing on the page can be changed this way right now".

name
name: string;

The name under the namespace: set-demand is served as <ns>.set-demand. Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens.

reversible?
optional reversible?: boolean;

True only when every covered entry is reversible; an entry that is not is left uncovered. Default false.

risk
risk: "low" | "medium" | "high";

The highest risk of any entry the action acts on. An entry whose own risk is higher is not covered: it is reported through onError and keeps its row in <ns>.observe without an affordance, so the published risk is never lower than a control's own ([P-HON-7]).

title
title: string;

What the action does, in the application's words ("Set a month's demand").

onResult()
onResult(ctx, result): Promise<void>;

Called by the server for every result of the bridge's actions ([S-AXE-14]); addProvider wires it, so there is nothing to pass to createAXE. A refusal the runtime made before an entry action's handler ran (a stale expectedRev under [S-AXE-4], an input that fails the schema, a missing idempotencyKey) is recorded in the caller's ledger with source: "server", the entry id and op the act would have had, and the actor of [S-AXE-3], when the runtime admitted the caller under the action's auth mode. Everything else is left alone: an act the surface saw is already in the ledger, and an unidentified caller of a protected action writes nothing.

Parameters
ctx

ProviderResultContext

result

Result

Returns

Promise<void>

Who is asking, as the AXE runtime established it: the input to a SurfaceResolver and to a scope key. identity is the authenticated user (null when anonymous), siteKey what verifySiteKey returned for a site action (null otherwise, and always null in an availability check), request the request being served (null when the manifest is described outside one).

domainActions()

function domainActions(source, options?): DomainBridge;

Derive the AXE actions for a surface as a fixed set of parameterized domain actions ([S-AXE-10]): <ns>.observe, <ns>.ledger, and one action per DomainActionSpec, each taking { entryId, text?, confirm? }. Every act goes through surface.act with the entry's own op, the envelope's expectedRev, and the same ladder, ledger, and action events as the per-control actions of surfaceActions. The set does not change as rows come and go, so the manifest and the MCP tool list stay the same size whatever the table holds; the rows, their availability, and the action that acts on each come from <ns>.observe.

Both granularities can serve one surface side by side under different namespaces.

Parameters

source

Surface | SurfaceResolver

options?

DomainActionsOptions = {}

entrySlug()

function entrySlug(entryId): string;

The plain slug of an entry id ([S-AXE-7]): lowercase; every run of characters outside a-z0-9 becomes one hyphen; leading and trailing hyphens are dropped; a slug that is empty or starts with a digit is prefixed with e- so it fits the action-name grammar ([P-ACT-1]).
